cells.tense: You are in it right now, and your hands are on the work.
cells.ask: Put the next hour on the thing that is actually yours, and when it holds, let one person see it before you move on.
cells.core:
You've got your hands on real weight and it isn't crushing you. The strength isn't dramatic. It's that you keep showing up to the thing that needs doing, and you do it with your own hands, the same way today as yesterday. That's the part people don't see, and it's the part holding the whole thing up.

What grows out of it is quieter than you'd expect. You're not doing this to be seen. You're doing it because it's yours. But somewhere underneath the persistence is a question you've been answering with your days: what are you, when nobody's watching? The work is starting to answer it. Where it bends is that you keep going without letting the answer land. Keep your hand on the thing, and let it land.
cells.sheetLine: Your hands are on it, and it's holding.
cells.verb: carrying what is yours through pressure without needing anyone to see it
cells.place: the room where what you already are stops being hidden and starts being shown

cells.tense: You are carrying tomorrow's weight before it has been handed to you.
cells.ask: Pick the one load that is yours today, and leave the rest where they lie.
cells.core:
You're bracing. In your mind the whole thing has already fallen apart, and you're testing your grip on weight that hasn't arrived. So it doesn't stop when the day ends. It comes home with you. It sits down at the table.

The strength is real. That's the problem. You've got enough of it to pre-load every bad ending, and all that guarding takes up the room where the good part was supposed to land. You keep thinking you're being careful. You're being early to a thing that hasn't happened. What you're becoming is already here, waiting for you to set something down. Not everything. One thing.

cells.tense: You were holding something once, and you are still in the place it left you.
cells.ask: Let one person who saw the effort tell you what they saw; receive it without handing it back.
cells.core:
You know how to hold. You proved that. You held more than people knew, there was no witness and no thanks, and you went on anyway. That's real. But you stopped expecting anything back. You stopped showing up to the thing you actually are, because the showing didn't seem to matter enough.

It isn't strength that ran out. It's the finish. The work had an end and you didn't get to cross it, because nobody ever said it was done. You're at a threshold that has moved on without you. What you are is still in there, waiting to come forward. The way through isn't more effort. It's letting one person name what you did, and letting it land.

cells.tense: You are already becoming what you are, and you are calling it just getting through.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you did this week that was actually yours, not the day's, and let the sentence stand.
cells.core:
Right now, in how you keep your word, in what you carry without making a show of it, in who you are when the room empties — that part is running. It's shaping you in real time, not someday after the pressure lets up.

But you don't call it that. You call it making it work, or getting through, or just what needs doing. It's going on and you're not taking it as yours. Somewhere under everything you've done, there's a hope that kept you moving, and you've been treating it like a schedule instead of what it is. That hope is the thing becoming you. Say so, once.
cells.sheetLine: It's becoming you right now. Not someday.
